Visible

/VIZ-uh-buhl/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Visible means able to be seen

From the top of the tower, the entire coastline was clearly visible for miles in every direction.

Worked Example

On the clearest nights of the year, when the city finally cuts enough streetlights during a planned outage, thousands of stars that are normally lost to light pollution become visible to the naked eye all at once.

The stars were always there — city lights simply overpowered them. Removing that interference is all it took to make them visible again, which is exactly the word's simple, literal meaning: able to be seen.

How Visible Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

perceptible

perceptible: a more formal word, often used for things just barely able to be detected

observable

observable: emphasizes that something can be watched or studied directly

apparent

apparent: can mean visible, but often shifts toward 'obvious' or 'seemingly true'

Antonyms

invisible

invisible: the direct opposite — unable to be seen at all

hidden

hidden: deliberately or accidentally kept out of sight

How Strong Is It? — perceptible → apparent → visible

perceptible vs. visible

perceptible vs. visible: Something perceptible might be just barely detectable, at the edge of what the eye can register.

apparent vs. visible

apparent vs. visible: Something apparent is clearly noticeable, though the word can also drift toward meaning 'obvious' rather than strictly 'visible.'

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vis-

Root — vis-: to see (Latin videre/vis-)

Suffix — -ible

Suffix — -ible: capable of being

Put it together

Put it together: "Visible" literally means "capable of being seen" — the vis- root, from Latin videre, "to see," is one of the most productive roots in English, appearing in dozens of words about sight and observation.

Use the root in a new word: vision

Use the root in a new word: vision: After the surgery, her vision was sharper than it had been in twenty years.

Word Choice

neutral, literal or figurative

Visible is mostly literal (able to be physically seen), but it also appears figuratively, as in 'a visible improvement' or 'no visible means of support,' where it means clearly evident rather than literally seen with the eyes.
